questions.stem: (I) Penguins are birds that cannot fly. (II) Instead, their wings have evolved into flippers that make them excellent swimmers. (III) Polar bears live in the Arctic, far from any penguins. (IV) Some penguins can dive to depths of more than 500 metres. (V) Their dense feathers and a layer of fat keep them warm in icy water.
questions.explanation: Paragraf penguenlerin uyumunu anlatıyor; kutup ayısı cümlesi odak dışı ve V’deki ‘Their’ zincirini bozuyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Drinking enough water is essential for good health. (II) Water helps to regulate body temperature and remove waste. (III) Even mild dehydration can cause headaches and tiredness. (IV) Mineral water is sold in plastic or glass bottles. (V) Doctors therefore recommend drinking around two litres of water a day.
questions.explanation: Su içmenin sağlığa etkisi anlatılıyor; şişe türü ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World’s Fair in Paris. (II) Paris is also famous for its cafés and fashion. (III) At first, many artists criticised its design as ugly. (IV) However, it soon became a symbol of the city. (V) Today, it attracts about seven million visitors a year.
questions.explanation: Kulenin öyküsü ilerlerken Paris’in kafeleri konu dışı; IV’teki ‘it’ zinciri III’ye bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Many children today spend several hours a day in front of screens. (II) Experts warn that this can affect their sleep and physical activity. (III) Screens can also make it harder for children to concentrate. (IV) Televisions were first sold to the public in the 1930s. (V) Parents are therefore advised to limit their children’s screen time.
questions.explanation: Ekran süresinin etkileri anlatılıyor; televizyon tarihi ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Camels are well adapted to life in the desert. (II) They can go for long periods without drinking water. (III) Their humps store fat, which can be converted into energy. (IV) Long eyelashes also protect their eyes from sand. (V) Horses were domesticated in Central Asia.
questions.explanation: Develerin çöle uyumu; atların evcilleştirilmesi ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Moon has a strong influence on the Earth’s oceans. (II) Its gravity causes the rise and fall of the tides. (III) The first person to walk on the Moon was Neil Armstrong. (IV) Most coastal areas experience two high tides and two low tides each day. (V) Tides are especially strong when the Sun and Moon are aligned.
questions.explanation: Ay’ın gelgitlere etkisi; Armstrong bilgisi konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day. (II) It provides energy after a long night without food. (III) Studies suggest that children who eat breakfast concentrate better at school. (IV) A healthy breakfast should include fruit, grains and protein. (V) Some restaurants serve breakfast all day.
questions.explanation: Kahvaltının önemi; restoran servisi odak dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Bicycles are an environmentally friendly form of transport. (II) The Tour de France is a famous cycling race. (III) They produce no emissions and take up little space on the road. (IV) Cycling is also good for physical health. (V) For these reasons, many cities are building more cycle lanes.
questions.explanation: Bisikletin çevresel/sağlık faydası; yarış bilgisi akışı bozuyor ve V’deki ‘these reasons’ faydalara bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Volunteering can benefit both the community and the volunteer. (II) Volunteers help people in need, such as the elderly or the homeless. (III) Many companies pay their employees a monthly salary. (IV) At the same time, they gain new skills and make new friends. (V) Some studies even show that volunteering can improve mental health.
questions.explanation: Gönüllülüğün faydaları; maaş bilgisi ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Rainforests are home to more than half of the world’s plant and animal species. (II) They also produce a large share of the planet’s oxygen. (III) Unfortunately, rainforests are being cut down at an alarming rate. (IV) Deserts, on the other hand, receive very little rainfall. (V) This destruction threatens countless species with extinction.
questions.explanation: Yağmur ormanları anlatılıyor; çöllere geçiş akışı bozuyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Learning a foreign language opens many doors. (II) English uses the Latin alphabet. (III) It can improve job opportunities in an increasingly global economy. (IV) It also allows people to understand other cultures more deeply. (V) Moreover, research shows that learning languages keeps the brain active.
questions.explanation: Dil öğrenmenin faydaları; İngilizcenin alfabesi ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Owls are mainly active at night. (II) Their large eyes allow them to see well in low light. (III) They also have excellent hearing, which helps them locate prey in the dark. (IV) Special feathers allow owls to fly almost silently. (V) Eagles build their nests on high cliffs.
questions.explanation: Baykuşların gece avcılığına uyumu; kartal yuvası ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Traffic jams are a major problem in many large cities. (II) They waste time and fuel and increase air pollution. (III) Many people enjoy listening to music while driving. (IV) Some cities have introduced congestion charges to reduce traffic. (V) Others have invested heavily in public transport.
questions.explanation: Trafik sorunu ve çözümler; araba kullanırken müzik dinlemek konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Sleep deprivation affects far more than just our mood. (II) Research shows that people who sleep less than six hours a night are more likely to develop heart disease. (III) Lack of sleep also weakens the immune system, making people more vulnerable to infections. (IV) Many animals, such as bats, sleep for most of the day. (V) In addition, tired people are more likely to be involved in traffic accidents.
questions.explanation: Uykusuzluğun insan sağlığına etkileri; yarasaların uyku süresi bağlamdan kopuk.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The ancient Romans were skilled engineers. (II) The Roman Empire was eventually divided into eastern and western halves. (III) They built roads, bridges and aqueducts, many of which are still standing today. (IV) Their aqueducts carried water over long distances to supply cities. (V) Roman concrete, which hardened even under water, was stronger than many modern mixtures.
questions.explanation: Romalıların mühendisliği; imparatorluğun bölünmesi siyasi tarih, akış dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Social media has changed the way news is shared. (II) Stories can now reach millions of people within minutes. (III) However, false information can spread just as quickly as accurate reporting. (IV) Many social media users post photos of their holidays. (V) As a result, many experts argue that media literacy should be taught in schools.
questions.explanation: Haberin yayılması ve yanlış bilgi; tatil fotoğrafları odağı kaydırıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Glaciers are melting faster than at any time in recorded history. (II) This contributes to rising sea levels, which threaten coastal communities. (III) Glaciers also supply fresh water to millions of people during the dry season. (IV) As they shrink, these communities may face serious water shortages. (V) Skiing is a popular winter sport in the Alps.
questions.explanation: Buzulların erimesinin sonuçları; kayak sporu ilgisiz ve IV’deki ‘these communities’ III’e bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognise specific germs. (II) They usually contain weakened or inactive parts of a virus or bacterium. (III) Some diseases, such as the common cold, are caused by many different viruses. (IV) When a vaccinated person is later exposed to the real germ, the body can fight it off quickly. (V) This is why vaccines have been so successful in controlling diseases like measles.
questions.explanation: Aşının çalışma mekanizması; soğuk algınlığı cümlesi akışı bozuyor, V’deki ‘This’ IV’e bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Urbanisation has increased rapidly over the past century. (II) Today, more than half of the world’s population lives in cities. (III) Cities offer better access to jobs, education and health care. (IV) However, rapid growth can also lead to overcrowding and pollution. (V) Many farmers use modern machinery to increase their yields.
questions.explanation: Kentleşme ve sonuçları; tarım makineleri konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Chess has been played for more than 1,500 years. (II) Some players memorise thousands of opening moves. (III) The game is thought to have originated in India. (IV) It later spread to Persia and then to Europe, where the modern rules developed. (V) Today, it is played by millions of people around the world, both in person and online.
questions.explanation: Satrancın tarihsel yayılımı kronolojik ilerliyor; ezber cümlesi zinciri kesiyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Noise pollution is an often overlooked environmental problem. (II) Long-term exposure to traffic noise has been linked to high blood pressure and stress. (III) Classical music is said to help plants grow. (IV) It can also disturb sleep, even if people do not wake up. (V) Some cities now use noise barriers and quieter road surfaces to reduce the problem.
questions.explanation: Gürültü kirliliğinin etkileri ve çözümler; bitkilere müzik konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Silk Road was a network of trade routes connecting East and West. (II) Merchants carried silk, spices and precious metals along these routes. (III) Ideas, religions and technologies also travelled along the Silk Road. (IV) Silkworms feed almost exclusively on mulberry leaves. (V) In this way, it played a crucial role in the development of many civilisations.
questions.explanation: İpek Yolu’nun ticari ve kültürel rolü; ipek böceğinin beslenmesi odağı kaydırıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Many people suffer from a fear of public speaking. (II) Some of the greatest speeches in history were given by politicians. (III) Symptoms can include a racing heart, sweating and a shaking voice. (IV) Fortunately, this fear can often be reduced through preparation and practice. (V) Breathing exercises can also help speakers stay calm.
questions.explanation: Konuşma korkusu ve başa çıkma yolları; tarihî konuşmalar konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Artificial sweeteners are used in many ‘diet’ products. (II) They provide a sweet taste with few or no calories. (III) However, some studies suggest that they may increase cravings for sweet foods. (IV) As a result, their effect on weight loss remains uncertain. (V) Sugar cane is grown mainly in tropical regions.
questions.explanation: Yapay tatlandırıcıların etkisi; şeker kamışının yetiştiği yer ilgisiz ve III’teki ‘they’ zincirini bozuyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Coffee is one of the most widely traded goods in the world. (II) Millions of small farmers depend on it for their income. (III) Many people add sugar or milk to their coffee. (IV) However, coffee prices can change dramatically from year to year. (V) This makes the livelihoods of coffee farmers very insecure.
questions.explanation: Kahvenin ekonomisi ve çiftçilerin güvencesizliği; kahveye süt eklemek ilgisiz, V’deki ‘This’ IV’e bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The human skin is the body’s largest organ. (II) It protects internal organs from injury and infection. (III) It also helps to regulate body temperature through sweating. (IV) Many cosmetic products claim to reduce wrinkles. (V) In addition, nerve endings in the skin allow us to feel touch, heat and pain.
questions.explanation: Derinin işlevleri; kozmetik iddiaları konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Earthquakes occur when the plates that make up the Earth’s crust move suddenly. (II) Volcanoes are also popular tourist attractions in some countries. (III) Most earthquakes happen along the boundaries between these plates. (IV) Japan and Turkey, for example, lie in highly active zones. (V) Earthquake-resistant buildings can save thousands of lives.
questions.explanation: Depremlerin oluşumu ve etkileri; volkanların turistik oluşu konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Minimalism is a lifestyle that focuses on owning fewer possessions. (II) Its supporters claim that having less stuff reduces stress and saves money. (III) They also argue that it allows people to spend more time on experiences rather than things. (IV) Minimalist art became popular in New York in the 1960s. (V) Critics, however, point out that minimalism is often a choice available only to the wealthy.
questions.explanation: Yaşam tarzı olarak minimalizm; sanat akımı farklı bir konu.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The concept of ‘food miles’ refers to the distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is consumed. (II) Many consumers assume that locally grown food is always better for the environment. (III) However, studies show that transport accounts for only a small part of food’s total carbon footprint. (IV) Tomatoes grown in heated greenhouses nearby, for instance, may produce more emissions than those imported from warmer countries. (V) Local markets are also valued as places where people can meet and socialise.
questions.explanation: Paragraf gıda milinin çevresel etkisini sorguluyor; pazarların sosyal değeri odağı karbon ayak izinden uzaklaştırıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Placebo effect has long fascinated researchers. (II) In clinical trials, patients who receive inactive pills often report real improvements. (III) The pharmaceutical industry is one of the most profitable sectors of the global economy. (IV) This makes it necessary to compare new drugs against placebos rather than against no treatment at all. (V) Only if a drug performs significantly better than a placebo can it be considered effective.
questions.explanation: Plasebo ve klinik deneme mantığı; sektör kârlılığı akışı bozuyor, V IV’ü tamamlıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Language shapes the way we perceive colours, according to some researchers. (II) Russian speakers, for example, have separate basic words for light blue and dark blue. (III) Experiments show that they can distinguish between these shades slightly faster than English speakers. (IV) Such findings suggest that the categories provided by our language can influence perception. (V) Russian is written in the Cyrillic alphabet, which was developed in the ninth century.
questions.explanation: Dilin renk algısına etkisi; Kiril alfabesinin tarihi ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Microplastics are tiny plastic particles less than five millimetres long. (II) Plastic was first developed in the early twentieth century as a substitute for natural materials. (III) They have been found in oceans, rivers, soil and even the air we breathe. (IV) Recent studies have also detected them in human blood and lungs. (V) Scientists are now investigating what long-term effects this exposure may have on human health.
questions.explanation: Mikroplastiklerin yayılımı ve sağlık etkisi; plastiğin icadı akışı kesiyor, V’deki ‘this exposure’ IV’e bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Behavioural economics challenges the traditional assumption that people always make rational choices. (II) It shows, for example, that people value losses more heavily than equivalent gains. (III) Economics became an academic discipline in the nineteenth century. (IV) Similarly, the way a choice is presented can strongly influence decisions. (V) Governments have begun to use these insights to design policies that encourage healthier or more sustainable behaviour.
questions.explanation: Davranışsal iktisadın bulguları ve uygulamaları; iktisadın akademik tarihi konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Black Death, which swept through Europe in the fourteenth century, killed about a third of the population. (II) The resulting labour shortage gave surviving workers greater bargaining power. (III) In many regions, wages rose and the feudal system began to weaken. (IV) The disease was caused by a bacterium carried by fleas living on rats. (V) Some historians therefore see the plague as a turning point in European social history.
questions.explanation: Vebanın toplumsal-ekonomik sonuçları anlatılıyor; hastalığın biyolojik nedeni akışı bozuyor, V ‘therefore’ ile III’e bağlanıyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Some scientists argue that boredom has an important function. (II) The word ‘boredom’ first appeared in English in the nineteenth century. (III) It signals that our current activity is no longer rewarding. (IV) This may motivate us to seek new goals and experiences. (V) Modern technology, with its endless stream of entertainment, has made boredom less common.
questions.explanation: Can sıkıntısının işlevi ve günümüzdeki azalışı; kelimenin tarihi etimolojik ayrıntı, akış dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Nuclear power produces very little carbon dioxide during operation. (II) For this reason, some environmentalists now support it as a way of fighting climate change. (III) Critics, however, point to the risks of accidents and the problem of storing radioactive waste. (IV) The debate is likely to continue as countries search for alternatives to fossil fuels. (V) Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes for her research on radioactivity.
questions.explanation: Nükleer enerji tartışması; Curie’nin ödülleri konu dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Crowdsourcing involves obtaining ideas or services from a large group of people, usually online. (II) Wikipedia is perhaps the best-known example. (III) The internet was originally developed for military communication. (IV) Scientists have also used crowdsourcing to classify galaxies and fold proteins. (V) Such projects show that non-experts can make valuable contributions to research.
questions.explanation: Kitle kaynak kullanımı örnekleri; internetin askeri kökeni odak dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) The Mediterranean diet is associated with a lower risk of heart disease. (II) It is rich in vegetables, fruit, olive oil and fish, and low in red meat. (III) Researchers believe that its high content of unsaturated fats plays a key role. (IV) Olive trees can live for more than a thousand years. (V) Regular meals shared with family and friends, another feature of the diet, may also have health benefits.
questions.explanation: Akdeniz diyetinin sağlık etkileri; zeytin ağacının ömrü ilgisiz.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Procrastination is often mistaken for laziness. (II) Laziness is considered one of the seven deadly sins in Christian tradition. (III) Psychologists, however, see it mainly as a problem of emotional regulation. (IV) People put off tasks that make them feel anxious or bored in order to feel better in the short term. (V) Strategies that reduce negative feelings towards a task are therefore more effective than simply trying harder.
questions.explanation: Erteleme davranışının psikolojisi; tembelliğin dinî geleneği akış dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Invasive species are organisms introduced to areas where they do not naturally occur. (II) Without natural predators, they can spread rapidly and outcompete native species. (III) The cane toad, introduced to Australia in 1935, is a famous example. (IV) Australia is home to many unique animals, such as the kangaroo. (V) Originally brought in to control beetles, the toads spread across the continent and poisoned many native predators.
questions.explanation: İstilacı türler ve kara kurbağası örneği; kanguru cümlesi III–V zincirini kesiyor.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Carbon capture technology aims to remove carbon dioxide from the air or from industrial emissions. (II) The captured gas can then be stored underground or used in industrial processes. (III) Supporters see it as an essential tool for reaching climate targets. (IV) Critics, however, argue that it is expensive and may distract from the need to cut emissions. (V) Carbon is the fourth most abundant element in the universe.
questions.explanation: Karbon yakalama teknolojisi tartışması; karbonun evrendeki bolluğu akış dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Universal basic income is a policy in which every citizen receives a regular payment from the government. (II) Supporters argue that it would reduce poverty and give people more freedom to choose their work. (III) Income tax was first introduced in Britain in 1799 to pay for wars. (IV) Critics worry that it would be too expensive and might discourage people from working. (V) Several small-scale trials have been carried out to test these claims.
questions.explanation: Temel gelir tartışması; gelir vergisinin tarihi odak dışı.

questions.source_label: Özgün · YDS tarzı · Anlamı Bozan Cümle
questions.stem: (I) Sign languages are complete natural languages with their own grammar. (II) They are not simply gestures that represent spoken words. (III) British and American Sign Language, for example, are mutually unintelligible, even though both countries speak English. (IV) Like spoken languages, sign languages develop naturally within communities. (V) Many deaf people use hearing aids or cochlear implants.
questions.explanation: İşaret dillerinin dil olarak yapısı; işitme cihazları konu dışı.

questions.stem: Honey is one of the few foods that never goes bad. ---- In fact, archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still perfectly edible after thousands of years. This is because honey contains very little water and is naturally acidic, which prevents bacteria from growing.
options: Bees produce honey from the nectar of flowers.
If it is stored properly, it can last for centuries.
Honey is more expensive than it used to be.
Many people prefer sugar to honey in their tea.
Some people are allergic to bee stings.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘In fact … thousands of years’ bozulmama fikrini örnekliyor; boşluk yüzyıllarca dayanıklılığı söylemeli.

questions.stem: Many cities are introducing bicycle-sharing schemes. ---- Users can pick up a bike at one station and leave it at another, paying only for the time they use it. Supporters say these schemes reduce traffic and pollution.
options: Many people cannot ride a bicycle.
The first bicycle was invented in the nineteenth century.
Cycling in the rain can be dangerous.
Cars are still the most popular form of transport.
These systems allow people to rent bicycles for short journeys.
questions.explanation: Sonraki cümle sistemin nasıl çalıştığını anlatıyor; boşluk sistemi tanıtmalı (‘These systems’).

questions.stem: Sleep plays an important role in learning. During sleep, the brain processes the information it has received during the day. ---- For this reason, students who stay up all night before an exam often perform worse than those who get a good night’s sleep.
options: Some animals sleep for only a few hours a day.
Many people drink coffee to stay awake.
Beds should be replaced every ten years.
It also stores new memories so that they can be recalled later.
Dreams can sometimes be very strange.
questions.explanation: ‘For this reason’ öğrenme-uyku bağını sonuca bağlar; boşluk beyin işlevini sürdürmeli (It also…).

questions.stem: The Great Wall of China was not built all at once. ---- Most of the wall that tourists see today was built during the Ming dynasty, between the fourteenth and seventeenth centuries.
options: Millions of tourists visit Beijing every year.
It was constructed in different sections over a period of more than two thousand years.
China is one of the largest countries in the world.
The wall was built to protect trade routes only.
It is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
questions.explanation: ‘not built all at once’ fikrini açıklayan cümle: farklı bölümler, uzun süre.

questions.stem: Plastic bags are a serious threat to marine life. Sea turtles, for example, often mistake them for jellyfish, which they eat. ---- As a result, many countries have banned or taxed single-use plastic bags.
options: Most plastic is made from oil.
When they swallow the bags, the animals can suffer injury or death.
Jellyfish live in all the world’s oceans.
Sea turtles can live for more than fifty years.
Paper bags are also used in many shops.
questions.explanation: ‘As a result’ zararın sonucu; boşluk yutmanın zararını söylemeli.

questions.stem: ---- It is found in foods such as milk, cheese and yoghurt. Without enough of it, bones can become weak and break easily.
options: Calcium is essential for healthy bones and teeth.
Vitamin C is found in fruit.
Many people do not like the taste of milk.
Cheese is made in many different countries.
questions.explanation: ‘It is found in milk, cheese …’ ve ‘Without enough of it’ bir besin öğesini gerektiriyor: kalsiyum.

distractor_rationales.2: ‘it’ milk olur; ‘without enough of it bones weak’ uymaz

questions.stem: The city has decided to plant ten thousand new trees. ---- They also provide shade, which helps to keep streets cooler in summer.
options: Some people are allergic to pollen.
Trees improve air quality by absorbing pollutants.
The trees will be planted in spring.
The project will cost a lot of money.
Many trees were cut down last year.
questions.explanation: ‘They also provide shade’ ağaçların bir faydasından sonra gelir.

questions.stem: Octopuses are highly intelligent animals. They can solve puzzles, open jars and even escape from their tanks in aquariums. ----
options: Jars are usually made of glass.
Some scientists believe they are among the most intelligent invertebrates.
questions.explanation: Sonuç cümlesi zekâ fikrini tamamlamalı.

questions.stem: Working from home has several advantages. Employees save time and money because they do not have to travel to the office. ---- However, some people feel lonely and find it difficult to separate work from their private lives.
options: Offices are usually located in city centres.
Many people do not enjoy their jobs.
They can also organise their working hours more flexibly.
Travelling to work can be tiring.
Some companies do not allow working from home.
questions.explanation: ‘However’ öncesi avantaj listesi sürmeli: ek avantaj (also).

questions.stem: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world. ---- Despite these harsh conditions, a variety of plants and animals have adapted to survive there.
options: Deserts are found on every continent.
It is located in the north of Africa.
Many tourists visit Egypt every year.
Temperatures can reach over fifty degrees Celsius, and rain is extremely rare.
questions.explanation: ‘these harsh conditions’ boşlukta zor koşulların sayılmasını gerektirir.

questions.stem: Learning a musical instrument has many benefits for children. It improves their memory and concentration. ---- It also teaches them patience, as learning to play well takes years of practice.
options: In addition, it can help them to develop better coordination.
Music lessons are given at school.
Many famous musicians started playing late.
questions.explanation: Faydalar listesi: ‘In addition’ ile ek fayda.

questions.stem: Volcanoes can be very destructive. ---- On the other hand, volcanic soil is extremely fertile, which is why many farmers live close to active volcanoes.
options: Volcanoes are found under the sea too.
Eruptions can destroy towns and kill thousands of people.
Farmers grow many kinds of crops.
questions.explanation: ‘On the other hand’ olumsuz bir örnekten sonra gelir: yıkım.

questions.stem: Many people believe that goldfish have a memory of only three seconds. ---- In experiments, they have been trained to respond to sounds and to push levers to get food.
options: However, research has shown that they can remember things for months.
Some fish can live for a very long time.
questions.explanation: Yaygın inanç → ‘However’ ile düzeltme → deney kanıtı.

questions.stem: Chocolate is made from the seeds of the cacao tree. ---- They are then fermented, dried and roasted before being ground into a paste.
options: Dark chocolate may be good for health.
Chocolate is popular all over the world.
First, the seeds are removed from the pods of the tree.
Cacao trees grow in hot climates.
questions.explanation: ‘They are then …’ bir süreç adımı ister: ‘First …’.

questions.stem: Public libraries are changing. ---- Today, many of them also offer free internet access, language courses and community events.
options: In the past, they were mainly places to borrow books.
Many books are now available online.
questions.explanation: ‘Today …’ karşılaştırması ‘In the past …’ ile kurulur.

questions.stem: For centuries, people believed that the brain stopped developing after childhood. ---- Experiments have shown that the adult brain can form new connections throughout life, especially when a person learns a new skill. This ability, known as neuroplasticity, has important implications for the treatment of brain injuries.
options: Many scientists have studied the heart as well.
Recent research, however, has challenged this view.
Brain injuries are common among athletes.
Children learn languages more quickly than adults.
The brain uses about twenty percent of the body’s energy.
questions.explanation: Eski inanç → ‘however’ ile itiraz → deney kanıtı zinciri.

questions.stem: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. ---- They provide food and shelter for about a quarter of all marine species. However, rising sea temperatures are causing widespread coral bleaching.
options: Yet they are among the most biologically diverse ecosystems on Earth.
The Great Barrier Reef is in Australia.
Corals are actually animals, not plants.
Coral bleaching was first reported in the 1980s.
questions.explanation: ‘less than one percent’ ile ‘Yet … most diverse’ karşıtlığı kurulur; sonraki cümle çeşitliliği açıklar.

questions.stem: Some economists argue that a four-day working week would increase productivity. They point out that tired employees make more mistakes and work more slowly. ---- Critics, on the other hand, warn that some businesses, such as hospitals, cannot easily reduce working hours.
options: A shorter week, they say, would allow workers to rest and return to work more focused.
Hospitals are open twenty-four hours a day.
Many people work more than fifty hours a week.
The five-day week was introduced in the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: Destekçilerin gerekçesi tamamlanmalı (they say), sonra ‘Critics’ gelir.

questions.stem: The printing press, invented around 1440, transformed European society. Before its invention, books were copied by hand and were extremely expensive. ---- This helped to spread new ideas quickly and contributed to the rise of literacy.
options: Gutenberg was a goldsmith by profession.
The first printed book was the Bible.
With the new technology, books could be produced faster and more cheaply.
questions.explanation: ‘This helped to spread ideas’ ucuz ve hızlı üretime gönderme yapar.

questions.stem: Bilingual children often perform better on tasks that require switching between different rules. ---- This constant practice appears to strengthen the brain’s ability to control attention.
options: Many countries have more than one official language.
Some tasks are more difficult than others.
This may be because they are used to switching between two languages every day.
Learning a second language is difficult for adults.
Children should start school at the age of six.
questions.explanation: ‘This constant practice’ her gün dil değiştirmeye gönderme yapar.

questions.stem: In the nineteenth century, cholera killed millions of people in Europe. Doctors believed the disease was spread through ‘bad air’. ---- By mapping the cases, he showed that they were clustered around a single contaminated water pump.
options: In 1854, however, the London doctor John Snow suspected that water was the real source.
Many doctors refused to wash their hands.
Air pollution was a serious problem in London.
Cholera is still a problem in some parts of the world.
questions.explanation: ‘he showed …’ zamiri bir kişinin tanıtılmasını gerektirir: John Snow.

questions.stem: Electric cars produce no exhaust emissions. ---- If the electricity used to charge them comes from coal-fired power stations, their overall impact on the environment may be smaller than expected.
options: Charging stations are becoming more common.
Many governments offer subsidies for electric cars.
However, they are not necessarily as clean as they seem.
They are also much quieter than petrol cars.
The first electric cars were built in the 1800s.
questions.explanation: Sonraki cümle bir sınırlama getiriyor; boşluk ‘However … not necessarily clean’ olmalı.

questions.stem: Deserts are not always hot. ---- Antarctica, for example, receives less precipitation than the Sahara, even though it is covered in ice.
options: Some deserts have large sand dunes.
A desert is defined by how little rain it receives, not by its temperature.
The Sahara is growing larger every year.
Ice covers about ten percent of the Earth’s land.
questions.explanation: Antarktika örneği tanımı (yağış) açıklar.

questions.stem: Many people assume that multitasking allows them to get more done. ---- Studies show that switching between tasks reduces efficiency and increases the number of errors.
options: Women are often said to be better at multitasking.
In reality, the brain cannot focus on two demanding tasks at the same time.
questions.explanation: Varsayım → gerçek (In reality) → çalışma kanıtı.

questions.stem: The Vikings are often remembered as violent raiders. ---- They established trade routes that stretched from North America to the Middle East and founded towns such as Dublin.
options: However, they were also skilled traders, explorers and settlers.
Their ships were fast and light.
questions.explanation: Klişe → ‘However … traders’ → ticaret örnekleri.

questions.stem: Tea was first introduced to Britain in the seventeenth century. At first, it was an expensive luxury enjoyed only by the rich. ---- By the nineteenth century, it had become the national drink.
options: The British Empire was very large.
Coffee houses were also popular at that time.
Over time, however, prices fell and tea became popular among all social classes.
Tea is grown mainly in China and India.
Some people add milk to their tea.
questions.explanation: Lüks → zamanla ucuzlama → ulusal içecek sıralaması.

questions.stem: Honeybees communicate through a ‘waggle dance’. ---- The direction of the dance shows the direction of the food relative to the sun, while its length indicates the distance.
options: A colony can contain thousands of bees.
Some people keep bees in their gardens.
By performing this dance, a bee can tell others where to find flowers.
questions.explanation: Dansın işlevi (yer bildirmek) → yön ve mesafe detayları.

questions.stem: Some species of trees can communicate with each other through underground networks of fungi. ---- In this way, older trees can help young trees growing in the shade to survive.
options: Some trees live for thousands of years.
Mushrooms are a type of fungus.
Fungi are neither plants nor animals.
Forests cover about a third of the Earth’s land.
Through these networks, they can share nutrients and send warning signals.
questions.explanation: ‘In this way’ besin paylaşımına gönderme yapar.

questions.stem: Urban gardens have become popular in many cities. They provide fresh vegetables for local residents. ---- Moreover, they bring neighbours together and create a sense of community.
options: Some people do not like gardening.
Many gardens were destroyed during the war.
They can also reduce the heat in cities by replacing concrete with plants.
Vegetables are more expensive in cities.
questions.explanation: Fayda zinciri: ‘also’ + ‘Moreover’.

questions.stem: Sharks have existed for more than 400 million years. ---- Today, however, many shark species are threatened with extinction because of overfishing.
options: Sharks have several rows of teeth.
They survived several mass extinctions, including the one that killed the dinosaurs.
Shark fin soup is popular in some countries.
There are more than 500 species of shark.
Some sharks can swim very fast.
questions.explanation: Dayanıklılık (geçmiş) ↔ ‘Today, however’ tehdit karşıtlığı.

questions.stem: For a long time, the decline of the Maya civilisation was attributed to warfare and political instability. ---- Analysis of lake sediments shows a series of severe droughts between 800 and 1000 AD, precisely when many Maya cities were abandoned. Nevertheless, most researchers agree that the collapse probably resulted from a combination of factors.
options: The Maya developed a sophisticated calendar.
More recent studies, however, point to climate change as a major factor.
Warfare was common among ancient civilisations.
Many Maya descendants still live in Central America.
Maya cities were built of stone.
questions.explanation: Eski açıklama → yeni çalışmalar (iklim) → tortu kanıtı → ‘Nevertheless … combination’.

questions.stem: The placebo effect is well documented in medicine. Patients who receive a sugar pill often report feeling better, even though the pill contains no active ingredient. ---- Remarkably, some studies have found that placebos can work even when patients are told they are taking one.
options: Many drugs have serious side effects.
Sugar pills are very cheap to produce.
Doctors are not allowed to lie to patients.
Researchers believe this happens because the patient’s expectations influence how the brain processes symptoms.
questions.explanation: Etkinin mekanizmasını (beklenti) açıklayan cümle; ‘Remarkably’ beklentiye rağmen işe yarayan durumu kontrast olarak getirir.

questions.stem: Many people believe that creativity is a rare gift possessed by only a few. ---- Moreover, it can be developed through practice, just like any other skill. Encouraging curiosity and allowing time for experimentation are among the most effective ways of doing so.
options: Some schools do not teach art.
Creativity is difficult to define precisely.
Psychologists, however, argue that everyone is capable of creative thinking.
Famous artists are often considered geniuses.
questions.explanation: ‘Moreover, it can be developed’ bir karşı görüşe ek yapar: herkes yaratıcı olabilir.

questions.stem: Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve so that drugs no longer kill them. ---- For example, patients often stop taking antibiotics as soon as they feel better, allowing the strongest bacteria to survive and multiply.
options: The overuse and misuse of antibiotics has greatly accelerated this process.
Viruses cannot be treated with antibiotics.
Some bacteria are beneficial to health.
questions.explanation: ‘For example’ kötü kullanım örneği verir; boşluk ‘misuse’ fikrini içermeli.

questions.stem: Early explorers of the Arctic often suffered from scurvy, a disease caused by a lack of vitamin C. ---- The Inuit, however, rarely developed the disease. Researchers later discovered that raw seal and whale meat, which formed a large part of their diet, contains small but sufficient amounts of the vitamin.
options: Many explorers died on their journeys.
The Arctic is one of the coldest places on Earth.
Vitamin C is found in oranges and lemons.
The Inuit built houses from snow.
Their diets consisted mainly of preserved foods, with few fresh fruits or vegetables.
questions.explanation: Kaşiflerin beslenmesi ↔ ‘The Inuit, however’ karşıtlığı; beslenme vurgusu.

questions.stem: The Industrial Revolution brought enormous economic growth. ---- Workers, including children, often laboured for fourteen hours a day in dangerous conditions for very low wages. It was only gradually, through reforms and the rise of trade unions, that these conditions improved.
options: Many new inventions appeared at this time.
Steam engines were used to power factories.
Cities grew rapidly during this period.
It began in Britain in the eighteenth century.
Yet this growth came at a high human cost.
questions.explanation: Büyüme ↔ ‘Yet … human cost’ → işçi koşulları detayları.

questions.stem: It is often assumed that the ability to use tools is unique to humans. ---- Chimpanzees use sticks to extract termites from their nests, and some crows can even bend wire into hooks to reach food.
options: Tools have become more complex over time.
Humans started using stone tools about three million years ago.
Observations of animals in the wild, however, have shown that this is not the case.
Chimpanzees share about ninety-eight percent of our DNA.
Crows are found on every continent except Antarctica.
questions.explanation: Varsayım → karşı gözlem → örnekler.

questions.stem: Languages are disappearing at an alarming rate. Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken today, nearly half may disappear by the end of this century. ---- Linguists are therefore working with communities to record and revive endangered languages before it is too late.
options: Latin is no longer spoken as a first language.
When a language dies, a unique way of understanding the world is lost with it.
English is the most widely studied foreign language.
Some languages have no written form.
Children learn their first language very quickly.
questions.explanation: ‘therefore’ kayıp neden önemli ise onu takip eder: kaybın değeri.

questions.stem: In many countries, the population is ageing rapidly. ---- This places a growing burden on pension systems, since fewer workers must support more retirees. Some governments have responded by raising the retirement age.
options: Young people are moving to cities.
People are living longer, while birth rates have fallen sharply.
Pensions were introduced in the nineteenth century.
Older people often have valuable experience.
questions.explanation: ‘This places a burden’ yaşlanmanın nedenlerini (uzun ömür + düşük doğum) gösteren cümleye gönderme yapar.

questions.stem: The idea that we use only ten percent of our brains is a popular myth. ---- Even during sleep, areas such as the frontal cortex remain active. Damage to almost any part of the brain, moreover, leads to some loss of function.
options: The brain weighs about one and a half kilograms.
The myth has appeared in several films.
Some people are more intelligent than others.
Brain scans show that we use virtually every part of the brain, even for simple tasks.
questions.explanation: Mit → karşı kanıt (tarama) → ‘Even during sleep’ genişletme.

questions.stem: Fast fashion allows consumers to buy the latest styles at very low prices. ---- The textile industry is one of the largest polluters in the world, and millions of tonnes of clothing end up in landfills every year.
options: Many clothes are produced in Asia.
Some brands are becoming more popular.
However, its environmental cost is enormous.
questions.explanation: Olumlu → ‘However … environmental cost’ → kirlilik kanıtları.

questions.stem: The Dunning–Kruger effect describes a tendency for people with limited knowledge in a field to overestimate their competence. ---- Experts, by contrast, are often more aware of what they do not know and therefore tend to underestimate their abilities.
options: Because they lack the knowledge needed to recognise their mistakes, they believe they are performing well.
The effect was first described in 1999.
Confidence is important in job interviews.
questions.explanation: Etkinin nedenini açıklar; ‘Experts, by contrast’ karşıtlığa geçer.

questions.stem: Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 after an absence of seventy years. ---- As a result, vegetation along riverbanks recovered, which in turn stabilised the banks and provided habitats for birds and beavers.
options: By hunting elk, they reduced overgrazing in many parts of the park.
Yellowstone was the first national park in the world.
Wolves live in packs of up to twenty animals.
Wolves are closely related to dogs.
questions.explanation: ‘As a result, vegetation recovered’ geyiklerin azalmasına bağlanır: trofik zincir.

questions.stem: Some historians argue that the most important invention of the twentieth century was not the computer but the shipping container. ---- By making the transport of goods much cheaper and faster, it made modern global trade possible.
options: The largest ships can carry thousands of containers.
Although it seems simple, it transformed the world economy.
Computers are used in every office.
Many ports are located in Asia.
questions.explanation: ‘By making … possible’ dönüşümü açıklar; boşluk ‘simple ama dönüştürücü’ fikrini kurar.

questions.stem: For decades, dietary fat was blamed for heart disease, and many people switched to low-fat products. ---- Researchers now believe that the type of fat matters more than the amount, and that sugar may play a greater role in heart disease than was once thought.
options: Unfortunately, many of these products contained large amounts of added sugar.
Heart disease is a leading cause of death.
Some people follow a vegetarian diet.
Olive oil is widely used in Mediterranean cooking.
questions.explanation: Düşük yağlı ürünler → şeker → ‘sugar may play a greater role’ zinciri.

questions.context: Many people think of bats as frightening creatures, but they play a very important role in nature. Around the world, there are more than 1,400 species of bats, and most of them eat insects. A single bat can eat thousands of mosquitoes in one night, which helps to control the spread of diseases such as malaria. Other bats feed on fruit and nectar. As they fly from plant to plant, they carry pollen and seeds, helping forests to grow. In fact, more than 500 plant species, including bananas and mangoes, depend on bats for pollination. Unfortunately, many bat populations are declining because of habitat loss and disease. Scientists warn that losing bats could have serious consequences for both farmers and ecosystems.

options: by carrying pollen from plant to plant
by eating large numbers of mosquitoes
by feeding on fruit and nectar

questions.context: The first public libraries in the modern sense appeared in the nineteenth century. Before that, most books were owned by churches, universities or wealthy individuals, and ordinary people had little access to them. The idea of a library that was free and open to everyone spread quickly, especially in Britain and the United States. The businessman Andrew Carnegie helped to fund more than 2,500 libraries around the world. Today, public libraries offer much more than books. Many provide free internet access, computer classes and activities for children. For people who cannot afford a computer at home, the library is often the only place where they can apply for jobs or access government services online.
questions.stem: According to the passage, before the nineteenth century ----.
options: every town had a free public library
ordinary people could rarely read the books owned by institutions and the rich
books were mostly owned by ordinary people
Andrew Carnegie opened the first library
questions.explanation: ‘ordinary people had little access to them.’

questions.context: Yawning is something almost all animals with a backbone do, from fish to humans. For a long time, people believed that we yawn because our bodies need more oxygen. However, experiments have not supported this idea: breathing extra oxygen does not reduce yawning. A more recent theory suggests that yawning helps to cool the brain. When we yawn, we take in a large amount of air, which may lower the temperature of the blood flowing to the head. This could explain why people yawn more when they are tired or bored, since the brain’s temperature tends to rise at these times. Interestingly, yawning is also contagious: seeing or even reading about someone yawning can make us yawn too.

options: is accepted by most scientists today
has not been confirmed by experiments
questions.explanation: ‘experiments have not supported this idea.’

questions.context: Many cities around the world are trying to make their streets safer for pedestrians. One popular approach is to lower speed limits. In Helsinki, for example, the speed limit on many streets was reduced to 30 kilometres per hour. In 2019, the city recorded no pedestrian deaths at all, which was a remarkable achievement for a capital city. Experts explain that the risk of death for a pedestrian hit by a car rises sharply with speed. At 30 kilometres per hour, most people survive a collision; at 50, the chances of survival are much lower. Lower speeds also make streets quieter and more pleasant for walking and cycling, which can encourage people to leave their cars at home.
questions.stem: Helsinki is given as an example of a city that ----.
options: has more pedestrians than any other city
reduced pedestrian deaths by lowering speed limits
banned cars from the city centre

questions.context: The so-called ‘Mozart effect’ became popular in the 1990s after a study reported that students performed better on spatial reasoning tasks after listening to a Mozart sonata. The media quickly exaggerated the findings, claiming that classical music could make babies more intelligent, and some governments even distributed classical music CDs to new parents. Later research, however, failed to replicate the original results consistently. Where improvements were found, they were small, lasted only a few minutes, and could also be produced by other music or by listening to a story, as long as the listener enjoyed it. The episode is often cited as an example of how scientific findings can be distorted as they move from the laboratory to the public.

questions.context: The notion that the tragedy of the commons is inevitable—that shared resources will always be overused because each individual has an incentive to take more than their share—was influentially set out by the ecologist Garrett Hardin in 1968. Hardin concluded that such resources must be either privatised or controlled by the state. The political economist Elinor Ostrom challenged this dichotomy. Studying fisheries, forests and irrigation systems around the world, she documented numerous communities that had managed common resources sustainably for centuries without either privatisation or central control. Their success, she argued, rested on locally devised rules, effective monitoring by the users themselves, graduated sanctions for rule-breakers and accessible mechanisms for resolving conflicts. Ostrom did not claim that self-governance always works; rather, she identified the conditions under which it is likely to succeed. Her work earned her the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2009, making her the first woman to receive the award.

questions.context: The discovery of Homo floresiensis on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003 forced palaeoanthropologists to reconsider some long-held assumptions. questions.context: Economists have long puzzled over what has been called the ‘productivity paradox’. Despite enormous investment in computers from the 1970s onwards, official statistics showed little improvement in productivity growth for nearly two decades. The economist Robert Solow famously remarked that one could see the computer age everywhere except in the productivity statistics. Several explanations have been proposed. One is that the benefits of a general-purpose technology take time to appear, because firms must first reorganise their work processes, retrain staff and develop complementary innovations; electricity, after all, took some forty years to transform factory production. Another is that conventional statistics fail to capture many of the gains, such as free online services whose value to consumers is not reflected in prices. A similar debate has now resurfaced around artificial intelligence, with optimists predicting a surge in productivity and sceptics pointing to the modest figures recorded so far.

questions.context: Contrary to the popular image of scientific discovery as the work of lone geniuses, historians of science increasingly emphasise its collective and contingent nature. The phenomenon of ‘multiple discovery’—in which the same finding is made independently by different people at roughly the same time—is strikingly common. Calculus was developed by both Newton and Leibniz; the theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed almost simultaneously by Darwin and Wallace; and the telephone was the subject of patent applications by Alexander Graham Bell and Elisha Gray on the very same day. The sociologist Robert Merton argued that such cases are not coincidences but the rule: once the necessary knowledge and tools are available, a discovery becomes, in a sense, ‘ripe’. This view does not deny the importance of individual talent, but it suggests that if a particular scientist had not made a given discovery, someone else probably would have done so before long.

questions.context: Contrary to the popular image of scientific discovery as the work of lone geniuses, historians of science increasingly emphasise its collective and contingent nature. The phenomenon of ‘multiple discovery’—in which the same finding is made independently by different people at roughly the same time—is strikingly common. Calculus was developed by both Newton and Leibniz; the theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed almost simultaneously by Darwin and Wallace; and the telephone was the subject of patent applications by Alexander Graham Bell and Elisha Gray on the very same day. The sociologist Robert Merton argued that such cases are not coincidences but the rule: once the necessary knowledge and tools are available, a discovery becomes, in a sense, ‘ripe’. This view does not deny the importance of individual talent, but it suggests that if a particular scientist had not made a given discovery, someone else probably would have done so before long.
questions.stem: According to Merton, a discovery becomes ‘ripe’ when ----.
options: two scientists compete with each other
the required knowledge and tools already exist
a genius decides to work on it
questions.explanation: ‘once the necessary knowledge and tools are available.’
